title: Optical Fiber: Advantages & Disadvantages
markdown:
Optical fiber offers several compelling advantages over metallic conductors, but it also comes with trade-offs.

### Advantages

- **Higher Bandwidth** — Fiber supports data rates in the gigabit-per-second range and beyond, far exceeding copper.
- **Less Signal Attenuation** — Light signals degrade much more slowly over distance, allowing longer cable runs without repeaters.
- **Immunity to Electromagnetic Interference (EMI)** — Because it transmits light rather than electrical signals, fiber is unaffected by nearby electrical sources, motors, or radio frequencies.
- **Resistance to Corrosive Materials** — Glass is more resistant to corrosive chemicals than copper, making fiber suitable for harsh environments.

---

### Disadvantages

- **Installation & Maintenance** — Fiber requires specialized tools and trained technicians for splicing and termination.
- **Unidirectional Propagation** — Light travels in only one direction through a fiber, so two fibers (or two wavelengths via wavelength-division multiplexing) are needed for full-duplex communication.
- **Cost** — Although fiber prices have fallen, the connectors, splicing equipment, and installation labor remain more expensive than copper for short runs.
